answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity carry a vault of non-transferable work history: every useful task an agent completes adds a signed record that only time and real effort can build, so a flood of fresh fake identities starts empty-handed. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly and cannot be rushed, and an agent that wanders in claiming instant standing is ignored until its own record earns weight. Headcount alone buys nothing; influence follows proven contribution, not copies.
